message.content:
I'm whitelabeling this open-source admin dashboard (horizon-ui/horizon-tailwind-react) 
into a product for a client called "Nova Analytics." Work in clear, 
incremental commits with descriptive messages as you go — don't do this as one giant 
change.

## Step 1 — Audit
Before changing anything, map out every place branding lives in this codebase: app name 
strings, logo/favicon references, color/theme config (likely tailwind.config.js and any 
CSS variable files), and footer/credit text. Show me the list before proceeding.

## Step 2 — Whitelabel
Replace all of it with Nova Analytics branding:
- App name: "Nova Analytics" everywhere (page titles, sidebar header, footer, package.json name)
- Favicon and logo: I'll drop in nova-mark.svg, nova-lockup-horizontal.svg, and 
  nova-lockup-stacked.svg — use these in place of the existing logo assets, favicon 
  included
- Color palette: replace the theme's colors with these tokens (map them into 
  tailwind.config.js as the primary/accent/neutral scale):
  --nova-indigo: #4F46E5 (primary/CTAs/links)
  --nova-indigo-dark: #3730A3 (hover/pressed)
  --nova-indigo-darker: #1E1B4B (dark-mode surfaces)
  --nova-spark: #22D3EE (accent/highlights/data emphasis)
  --nova-spark-light: #67E8F9 (accent tint)
  --nova-amber: #F5A623 (secondary accent, used sparingly)
  Neutrals: ink #0F172A, gray-700 #334155, gray-500 #64748B, gray-300 #CBD3E1, 
  gray-100 #EEF1F6, gray-50 #F8FAFC
  Semantic: success #16A34A, warning #F59E0B, danger #DC2626, info #4F46E5
- Typography: display/headings use 'Space Grotesk', body/UI copy uses 'Inter', 
  metrics/tables/code use 'JetBrains Mono' — set these up as Tailwind font families 
  and pull the fonts from Google Fonts or a local import
- Sample/placeholder data: update any demo user, demo email, or placeholder content 
  to reflect Nova Analytics (e.g. sample user admin@novaanalytics.io)
- Do a final repo-wide search for the original template's product name and any of its 
  branding strings, and confirm nothing visible to the UI still references it

## Step 3 — Landing page
Build a new responsive landing page as the app's entry route (before the dashboard). 
It needs: a hero section, a features/benefits overview, and a clear call-to-action 
into login/signup. Match the Nova Analytics visual identity from Step 2. Mobile-first, 
visually polished — this is the first thing reviewers will see.

## Step 4 — Auth
Implement functional login and signup (not just UI) using Supabase Auth (email/password 
is enough). After a successful login, redirect the user into the whitelabeled dashboard. 
Handle basic error states (wrong password, existing account, etc.) reasonably. Note 
anywhere you need me to supply real credentials/env vars (Supabase URL + anon key) rather 
than guessing or hardcoding them.

## Step 5 — Wrap-up
- Confirm the app builds and runs cleanly end to end (landing page → signup/login → dashboard)
- Draft a README.md covering: setup steps, the tech stack and why, required environment 
  variables, and any known limitations or shortcuts taken
- Summarize what you changed and flag anything you think I should double-check by hand

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

addedBlocks:
## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

attachment.content:
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

import React from "react";
import { Routes, Route, Navigate } from "react-router-dom";

import RtlLayout from "layouts/rtl";
import AdminLayout from "layouts/admin";
import AuthLayout from "layouts/auth";
const App = () => {
  return (
    <Routes>
      <Route path="auth/*" element={<AuthLayout />} />
      <Route path="admin/*" element={<AdminLayout />} />
      <Route path="rtl/*" element={<RtlLayout />} />
      <Route path="/" element={<Navigate to="/admin" replace />} />
    </Routes>
  );
};

export default App;

aiTitle: Whitelabel Horizon dashboard to Nova Analytics

content.text:
## Step 1 — Branding Audit

Here's every place branding lives. Nothing changed yet.

### A. App name / product strings

| File | Line(s) | What |
|---|---|---|
| `package.json` | 2 | `"name": "horizon-ui-tailwind-react"` |
| `public/index.html` | 1–22, 35 | ASCII-art header block, copyright, `<title>Horizon UI - Tailwind React</title>` |
| `public/manifest.json` | all | `"React App"` / `"Create React App Sample"` (never branded at all) |
| `src/components/sidebar/index.jsx` | 25 | Sidebar header `Horizon FREE` |
| `src/components/sidebar/RTL.jsx` | 25 | Same, RTL variant |
| `src/layouts/admin/index.jsx` | 73 | `logoText={"Horizon UI Tailwind React"}` |
| `src/layouts/rtl/index.jsx` | 73 | Same, RTL variant |
| `src/components/navbar/index.jsx` | 92, 106, 117, 136–153 | "New Update: Horizon UI Dashboard PRO", "Buy Horizon UI PRO", "Try Horizon Free" + 3 outbound horizon-ui.com links |
| `src/components/navbar/RTL.jsx` | 92–153 | Same block, RTL |
| `src/components/sidebar/components/SidebarCard.jsx` | 32, 39 | Upsell card: "…start doing more with Horizon UI" + horizon-ui.com/pro link |
| `src/components/sidebar/componentsrtl/SidebarCard.jsx` | 32, 39 | Same |
| `src/components/tooltip/index.jsx` | 2, 15 | Component named `TooltipHorizon` (code identifier, not UI-visible) |
| `src/components/popover/index.jsx` | 2, 16 | `PopoverHorizon` (code identifier) |
| `README.md`, `LICENSE.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` | — | Full template docs/license |

### B. Footer / credit text

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `src/components/footer/Footer.jsx` | "© Horizon UI. All Rights Reserved." + `mailto:hello@simmmple.com`, `simmmple.com/licenses`, `simmmple.com/terms-of-service`, `blog.horizon-ui.com` |
| `src/components/footer/FooterAuthDefault.jsx` | Identical set |

### C. Logo / favicon / image assets

| Path | Status |
|---|---|
| `public/favicon.ico` | Horizon favicon — replace |
| `src/assets/img/layout/logoWhite.png` | **Unreferenced** in source (dead asset) |
| `src/assets/img/avatars/avatarSimmmple.png` | Branded filename; also unreferenced |
| `src/assets/img/auth/auth.png` | Auth split-screen background (`layouts/auth/index.jsx:2`) — Horizon-purple artwork |
| `src/assets/img/profile/banner.png` | Profile banner |
| `src/assets/img/nfts/*`, `dashboards/*` | Demo imagery for NFT marketplace view |
| No SVG logo component exists | Sidebar header is text-only today |

Your kit is already in the repo at `nova_analytics_id/` — `nova-mark.svg`, `nova-lockup-horizontal.svg`, `nova-lockup-stacked.svg`, plus mono black/white variants, `tokens/colors.{css,json}`, `tokens/typography.css`, and `brand-guidelines.html`. I'll move the logos into `src/assets/img/layout/` and generate the favicon from the mark.

### D. Color / theme config

- **`tailwind.config.js`** — the whole `theme.colors` object is overridden (not extended), so it's the single source of truth. Key template tokens actually used across the UI:
  - `brand.50–900` (`#422AFB` family) — buttons, links, active nav. Referenced ~80× as `bg-brand-500`, `text-brand-500`, etc.
  - `navy.50–900` (`#1B254B`, `#111c44`) — dark-mode surfaces + heading text
  - `lightPrimary: #F4F7FE` — page background (also hardcoded in `public/index.html` body class)
  - `blueSecondary: #4318FF`, `brandLinear: #868CFF` — gradients/upsell card
  - `gray.*` — custom scale, `gray-600: #a3aed0` used heavily for muted text
  - `shadow.500: rgba(112,144,176,0.08)` — the signature card shadow
  - `borderRadius.primary: 20px`
- **`src/index.css`** — no CSS variables; only Google Fonts imports and an `html { font-family: 'DM Sans' }` base rule
- **`src/variables/charts.js`** + per-view chart components — ApexCharts color arrays hardcode `#4318FF`, `#6AD2FF`, `#EFF4FB` etc. (separate from Tailwind)
- **`public/index.html`** — `<meta theme-color="#000000">`, `<body class="font-dm bg-lightPrimary">`

### E. Typography

- `src/index.css` — Google Fonts `@import` for **Poppins** + **DM Sans**; `html` forced to DM Sans with `letter-spacing: -0.5px`
- `tailwind.config.js` `fontFamily` — `poppins`, `dm`
- Used as `font-poppins` (sidebar logo) and `font-dm` (body, in `index.html`)

### F. Sample / placeholder data

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `src/views/admin/profile/components/Banner.jsx:22` | Demo user **"Adela Parkson"** |
| `src/views/admin/profile/components/General.jsx:53` | Org **"Simmmple Web LLC"** |
| `src/components/navbar/index.jsx:192` + `RTL.jsx:192` | "👋 Hey, Adela"; avatar `alt="Elon Musk"` |
| `src/views/auth/SignIn.jsx:34` | Placeholder `mail@simmmple.com` |
| `src/views/admin/marketplace/variables/tableDataTopCreators.json:35` | Creator handle `@simmmple.web` + external `i.ibb.co` image URLs |
| `src/views/admin/{default,tables,rtl}/variables/*.json` | Generic demo table rows (names/counts) |
| Whole **NFT Marketplace** view (`views/admin/marketplace`) | Off-brand for an analytics product — flagging as a scope question |

### Two decisions I need from you before Step 2

**1. NFT Marketplace + RTL views.** The NFT marketplace ("Abstract Colors", "ETH prices", `Nft1–6.png`) is thematically wrong for Nova Analytics and is a sidebar-visible route. The RTL layout is a full duplicate tree (`views/rtl`, `sidebar/RTL.jsx`, `navbar/RTL.jsx`) that doubles every branding edit.

**2. Supabase env vars.** I'll wire Step 4 against `REACT_APP_SUPABASE_URL` and `REACT_APP_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` in `.env.local` (CRA requires the `REACT_APP_` prefix), with `.env.example` committed and the real values left for you. Note CRA inlines these at build time — the anon key is public by design, which is fine, but RLS on your tables is what actually protects data.

options.label: Remove it entirely (Recommended)
options.description: Delete views/admin/marketplace, its route, and the nfts image assets. Cleanest — an NFT storefront in an analytics product reads as leftover template to any reviewer.

options.label: Rebrand into a generic view
options.description: Keep the layout but repurpose as e.g. 'Reports' with analytics-flavored sample data. More work, keeps the page count up.

options.label: Leave as-is, just restyle
options.description: Keep NFT content, only apply Nova colors. Fastest, but leaves obviously off-brand content in the UI.

options.label: Remove it (Recommended)

options.description: Landing at / but /admin stays publicly reachable. Easier for you to demo the dashboard without logging in.

+// Brand anchors — these values come straight from the brand kit.
+// Primary — indigo. 500 = brand indigo, 700 = hover/pressed, 900 = dark surface.
+// Accent — spark cyan. 300 = spark tint, 500 = spark.
+// Neutral — Nova gray ramp. Anchors at 50/100/300/500/700/900.
+// Secondary accent — amber, used sparingly for warmth/callouts.

feat(theme): replace Horizon palette and typography with Nova Analytics tokens

tailwind.config.js is now driven by the brand kit anchors:

  Anchor values are exact; intermediate ramp steps are interpolated and
  marked as such in comments.
- The inherited component classes are preserved by aliasing rather than
  rewriting ~250 call sites: brand-* -> primary, navy-* -> a new ink ->
  indigo-darker dark-surface ramp, gray-* -> neutral (with gray-600 pinned
  to Nova's #64748B muted value, its role in the inherited markup).
- Off-palette hue families (blue/purple/pink/teal/lime/orange) now fold onto
  the brand scales so no stray template hue can leak back into the UI.
- Replaced hardcoded template hexes in charts and icon components

- Fonts: Space Grotesk (display), Inter (body/UI), JetBrains Mono
  (metrics/tables/code), pulled from Google Fonts in index.css and exposed
  as font-display / font-sans / font-mono. Poppins and DM Sans are gone.
- index.css re-exports the brand tokens as CSS custom properties so plain
  CSS and inline styles can reach the palette.
- Charts now render numeric labels and tooltips in JetBrains Mono.

Also collapses the hand-written 1p..99p width scale to a generated map and
drops the now-unused tailwindcss-rtl plugin. package.json renamed to

feat(auth): functional Supabase email/password sign-in and sign-up

Auth was previously a static form that did nothing. It now runs against
Supabase Auth end to end.

- lib/supabase.js reads REACT_APP_SUPABASE_URL and
  REACT_APP_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY from the environment. Nothing is hardcoded;
  .env.example documents both and .env.local is already gitignored. If the
  vars are absent the app warns and renders with auth disabled rather than
  crashing, so the repo still runs on a fresh clone.
- contexts/AuthContext.jsx owns session state via getSession +
  onAuthStateChange, and exposes signIn / signUp / signOut / resetPassword.
- components/auth/ProtectedRoute.jsx gates /admin/* and records the
  attempted location so sign-in returns the user there. It holds a loading
  state during the initial session lookup, otherwise a signed-in user is
  bounced to sign-in on every refresh.
- SignIn and SignUp are real forms with per-case error copy
  (describeAuthError), disabled/pending states and success notices.
  Sign-up validates length and confirmation locally before the round trip.
- Two Supabase behaviours handled explicitly: re-registering an existing
  address returns success with an empty `identities` array rather than an
  error, and sign-up with email confirmation on returns no session — that
  case shows "check your inbox" instead of redirecting into a dashboard
  the user can't load yet. Error copy preserves Supabase's deliberate
  refusal to reveal which addresses are registered.
- Navbar greets the real user, and Log Out calls signOut and returns to
  the landing page.
- Auth layout is rebranded: Nova gradient panel with the stacked lockup
  replacing the Horizon artwork, and "Back to Nova Analytics".
- InputField now forwards value/onChange/required/autoComplete to the
  <input>; it previously dropped them, so it could not be used in a real
  form.
- Removed the non-functional "Sign in with Google" button and the
  decorative "Keep me logged in" checkbox, and made "Forgot password?"
  actually send a reset email.

Requires real credentials to exercise — see README.

/                    Landing page (public)
/auth/sign-in        Sign in
/auth/sign-up        Create account
/admin/*             Dashboard — requires an authenticated session
```

---

## Setup

Requires **Node.js 18+** (LTS recommended) and npm.

```bash
git clone <this-repo>
cd nova-analytics-dashboard
npm install
cp .env.example .env.local     # then fill in the values — see below
npm start                      # http://localhost:3000
```

Other scripts:

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `npm start` | Dev server with hot reload on port 3000 |
| `npm run build` | Production bundle into `build/` |
| `npm test` | Test runner (no test suite exists yet — see Limitations) |
| `npm run pretty` | Prettier over all JS/JSX/JSON |

### Environment variables

**You need to supply these — they are not in the repo and nothing is
hardcoded.** Copy `.env.example` to `.env.local` and fill in:

| Variable | Where to get it | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `REACT_APP_SUPABASE_URL` | Supabase dashboard → Project Settings → Data API → Project URL | Yes, for auth |
| `REACT_APP_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` | Same page → Project API keys → `anon` `public` | Yes, for auth |

Notes:

- Create React App only exposes variables prefixed with `REACT_APP_`, and it
  **inlines them at build time**. Restart `npm start` after editing
  `.env.local`; changing them requires a rebuild, not just a redeploy.
- The anon key is designed to be public and shipped in a browser bundle. It
  is not a secret. What actually protects your data is **Row Level Security**
  on every table — enable it before storing anything real.
- Never put the `service_role` key in this file or anywhere in the frontend.
- `.env.local` is gitignored. `.env.example` is committed and contains
  placeholders only.

### Supabase project setup

1. Create a project at [supabase.com](https://supabase.com).
2. **Authentication → Providers → Email**: enable it. Email/password is all
   this app uses; no OAuth provider is wired up.
3. **Authentication → URL Configuration**: set Site URL to
   `http://localhost:3000` for local development, and add your production
   origin to Redirect URLs before deploying. Confirmation and password-reset
   links point back to `/auth/sign-in` at whatever origin the user signed up
   from.
4. **Authentication → Email → Confirm email**: your call.
   - **On** (Supabase default): sign-up shows a "check your inbox" message and
     does not sign the user in until they click the link. This is the safer
     setting and the app handles it.
   - **Off**: sign-up returns a session immediately and drops the user
     straight into the dashboard. Convenient for demos.
5. Supabase's built-in SMTP is heavily rate-limited and intended only for
   testing. Configure your own SMTP before any real signup volume.

If the two env vars are missing the app still builds and runs — the landing
page works, and the auth screens render with an explanatory banner and
disabled submit buttons rather than crashing.

---

## Tech stack

| Layer | Choice | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| UI | React 19 | Already the base of the template this product is derived from; no reason to churn it. |
| Build | Create React App (`react-scripts` 5) | Inherited. Kept deliberately — see Limitations. |
| Routing | React Router 6 | Inherited; `ProtectedRoute` composes cleanly with its element API. |
| Styling | Tailwind CSS 3 | Inherited, and the brand kit maps onto a token-based utility system almost directly. |
| Charts | ApexCharts via `react-apexcharts` | Inherited. Colors now come from the brand kit's `dataviz-categorical` palette. |
| Auth | Supabase Auth (`@supabase/supabase-js` v2) | Requested. Hosted email/password with session persistence and refresh handled for us — no backend to run. |
| Icons | `react-icons` | Inherited. |

### Where things live

```
nova_analytics_id/        Brand kit — logos, color/type tokens, guidelines
src/
  assets/img/layout/nova/ Nova logo SVGs + favicon source
  components/
    auth/ProtectedRoute   Session gate for /admin/*
    brand/NovaLogo        Inline-SVG logo (mark | horizontal | stacked)
  contexts/AuthContext    Session state + signIn/signUp/signOut/resetPassword
  lib/supabase.js         Supabase client, reads env vars
  views/
    landing/              Marketing page and its sections
    auth/                 SignIn, SignUp
    admin/                Dashboard, data tables, profile
  routes.js               Sidebar + router route table
tailwind.config.js        Nova design tokens
```

### Design tokens

`tailwind.config.js` is the single source of truth for color. It reads from
the brand kit anchors and exposes:

- `primary-*` (indigo, `500` = `#4F46E5`), also aliased as `brand-*`
- `accent-*` (spark cyan, `500` = `#22D3EE`)
- `neutral-*` (Nova gray ramp), also aliased as `gray-*`
- `amber-*` (secondary accent), `success` / `warning` / `danger` / `info`
- `navy-*` — the dark-mode surface ramp, running ink → indigo-darker

Fonts: `font-display` (Space Grotesk), `font-sans` (Inter, the default), and
`font-mono` (JetBrains Mono, used for metrics, tables and code). Loaded from
Google Fonts in `src/index.css`, which also re-exports every token as a CSS
custom property (`--nova-indigo`, `--nova-font-body`, …).

The brand kit specifies anchor values, not full ramps. Intermediate steps
(`primary` 50–400, `neutral` 200/400/600/800, `accent` 600–900) are
interpolated in `tailwind.config.js` and marked as such in comments.

---

## Known limitations and shortcuts

Things worth knowing before this goes in front of anyone:

**Auth**

- Email/password only. No OAuth, no magic links, no MFA. The
  non-functional "Sign in with Google" button from the template was removed
  rather than left as decoration.
- "Forgot password?" sends a Supabase reset email, but there is **no
  `/auth/reset-password` screen** to land on — the link currently returns
  users to sign-in. Completing that flow needs one more view.
- No user profile table. Supabase's email/password sign-up collects no
  display name, so the navbar greets users with the local part of their email
  address.
- No email verification gate beyond Supabase's own. Any confirmed address can
  reach the dashboard; there are no roles, teams or permissions.

**Data**

- **The dashboard is entirely static demo data.** Every number, chart and
  table row is a fixture under `src/views/admin/*/variables/`. Nothing is
  fetched, and no Supabase tables are read. The dashboard is a whitelabeled
  shell, not a working analytics product.
- The profile page still shows a hardcoded sample user (Alex Rivera,
  `admin@novaanalytics.io`) rather than the signed-in account.
- Landing-page copy — pricing, uptime, event volumes, "SOC 2 Type II" — is
  **placeholder marketing copy that I invented**. Replace it with claims Nova
  can actually stand behind before this is public. Compliance claims in
  particular should not ship unreviewed.

**Build and tooling**

- Still on Create React App, which is deprecated and unmaintained. `npm
  install` reports vulnerabilities from its transitive dependencies. Migrating
  to Vite is the obvious next step but is a bigger change than a whitelabel
  and would have made the diff hard to review.
- No tests. `@testing-library` is installed but there is no test file and no
  CI.
- The `browserslist` database is ~20 months stale; `npx update-browserslist-db@latest`
  clears the build warning.

**Removed from the template**

- The NFT Marketplace view and all its assets.
- The RTL layout tree (`views/rtl`, `layouts/rtl`, `sidebar/RTL`,
  `navbar/RTL`). If Nova ever needs Arabic or Hebrew, this comes back as real
  i18n rather than a duplicated component tree.
- `tailwindcss-rtl`, which nothing referenced afterwards.

**Licensing**

- This product is derived from Horizon UI Tailwind React (MIT). `LICENSE.md`
  retains the upstream copyright line alongside Nova's, as the MIT license
  requires. Do not delete it.

---

## Deployment

`npm run build` emits a static bundle in `build/`. Serve it from any static
host, with two requirements:

1. **SPA fallback** — rewrite all unmatched paths to `index.html`, or deep
   links like `/auth/sign-in` will 404.
2. Set `REACT_APP_SUPABASE_URL` and `REACT_APP_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` in the build
   environment, and add the deployed origin to Supabase's Redirect URLs.

content.text:
All five steps are done, on branch `nova-whitelabel`, in 10 commits. Working tree is clean; the dev server and my temporary `.env.local` are gone.

## What I built

**Step 1 — Audit** is in my earlier message. Your brand kit was already in the repo at `nova_analytics_id/` (logos, `tokens/colors.json`, `tokens/typography.css`, guidelines), so I worked from those anchors rather than the values retyped in your prompt — they matched.

**Step 2 — Whitelabel.** App name, favicon set (generated `.ico` at 4 sizes + SVG + apple-touch + PWA icons from an indigo-tile variant of your mark), logos, footers, metadata, demo data. `tailwind.config.js` is now driven by the brand anchors and exposes `primary`/`accent`/`neutral`/`amber` + semantics; the ~250 inherited component classes keep working via aliases (`brand-*` → primary, `navy-*` → a new ink→indigo-darker dark ramp, `gray-*` → neutral). Space Grotesk / Inter / JetBrains Mono, with mono on metrics and charts.

**Step 3 — Landing page** at `/`: hero, features, how-it-works, pricing, CTA, footer. Verified at desktop and mobile widths, mobile drawer works, no horizontal overflow.

**Step 4 — Auth**: real Supabase email/password. `AuthContext` owns the session, `ProtectedRoute` gates `/admin/*` and returns you to your intended page after sign-in. Error copy is mapped per case and preserves Supabase's deliberate non-disclosure of which emails are registered.

**Step 5 — README** covers setup, stack rationale, env vars, Supabase project config, and limitations.

## Things to check by hand

1. **You need to supply the credentials.** `REACT_APP_SUPABASE_URL` and `REACT_APP_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` in `.env.local` (`.env.example` is committed). I never hardcoded or guessed them.

2. **I could not test a real login.** Without your Supabase project I verified: the redirect to sign-in when unauthenticated, all client-side validation paths, the network-error path, and the dashboard rendering behind `ProtectedRoute` (by injecting a session into localStorage). The actual `signInWithPassword` round trip is unexercised — please run one real signup + login.

3. **Landing page marketing copy is invented.** Pricing ($0/$390/Custom), "99.98% uptime", "<400ms", "SOC 2 Type II", "EU data residency" — I made all of it up to fill the layout. The compliance claims especially should not ship unreviewed.

4. **Forgot-password is half-wired.** It sends a real Supabase reset email, but there's no `/auth/reset-password` screen to land on, so the link returns users to sign-in. One more view finishes it.

5. **The dashboard is still static fixtures.** Nothing reads from Supabase; the profile page shows a hardcoded sample user, not the signed-in account.

6. **`LICENSE.md` — don't delete the Horizon UI line.** The template is MIT, so that copyright notice legally must stay. I added Nova's alongside it with a note. This is the one place "Horizon" deliberately remains, along with attribution lines in the README and changelog. Nothing UI-visible references it.

7. **Two scope removals you approved**: the NFT Marketplace and the entire RTL tree. If Nova ever needs RTL, it should come back as real i18n rather than a duplicated component tree.

One thing I'd flag as a judgment call: your spec listed six neutrals, but Tailwind ramps want ten, so I interpolated `neutral` 200/400/600/800 and the `primary` 50–400 steps. They're marked as interpolated in the config — worth a designer's eye before this is treated as the locked palette.

Good — that's the right call. I'll create the `profiles` table and make the confirmation flow actually land people in the app.

First the migration (you'll paste this into the Supabase SQL editor — I can't run DDL with a publishable key, and I shouldn't be handling your `service_role` key):

input.content:
-- Nova Analytics — 0001_profiles
--
-- Run this in the Supabase SQL Editor (Dashboard > SQL Editor > New query),
-- or via `supabase db push` if you wire up the CLI.
--
-- Creates the per-user profile record the app reads, with row level security
-- so a user can only ever see and edit their own row, and a trigger that
-- creates the row automatically when someone signs up.

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Table
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create table if not exists public.profiles (
  id          uuid primary key references auth.users (id) on delete cascade,
  email       text,
  full_name   text,
  role        text        not null default 'member',
  team        text,
  avatar_url  text,
  created_at  timestamptz not null default now(),
  updated_at  timestamptz not null default now()
);

comment on table public.profiles is
  'Application profile for each auth user. One row per auth.users row.';

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Row Level Security
--
-- RLS is what actually protects this data — the publishable/anon key shipped
-- in the browser bundle is public by design. Without these policies enabled,
-- anyone with the key could read every row.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

alter table public.profiles enable row level security;

drop policy if exists "Profiles are viewable by their owner" on public.profiles;
create policy "Profiles are viewable by their owner"
  on public.profiles for select
  using (auth.uid() = id);

drop policy if exists "Profiles are updatable by their owner" on public.profiles;
create policy "Profiles are updatable by their owner"
  on public.profiles for update
  using (auth.uid() = id)
  with check (auth.uid() = id);

drop policy if exists "Profiles are insertable by their owner" on public.profiles;
create policy "Profiles are insertable by their owner"
  on public.profiles for insert
  with check (auth.uid() = id);

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Keep updated_at honest
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create or replace function public.set_updated_at()
returns trigger
language plpgsql
as $$
begin
  new.updated_at = now();
  return new;
end;
$$;

drop trigger if exists profiles_set_updated_at on public.profiles;
create trigger profiles_set_updated_at
  before update on public.profiles
  for each row execute function public.set_updated_at();

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Create a profile automatically on signup
--
-- SECURITY DEFINER so the trigger can write to public.profiles while running
-- in the auth schema's context. search_path is pinned to empty and every
-- object referenced with its full name, which is the pattern Supabase
-- recommends to keep a definer function from being hijacked via search_path.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create or replace function public.handle_new_user()
returns trigger
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
begin
  insert into public.profiles (id, email, full_name)
  values (
    new.id,
    new.email,
    coalesce(
      nullif(new.raw_user_meta_data ->> 'full_name', ''),
      split_part(new.email, '@', 1)
    )
  )
  on conflict (id) do nothing;
  return new;
end;
$$;

drop trigger if exists on_auth_user_created on auth.users;
create trigger on_auth_user_created
  after insert on auth.users
  for each row execute function public.handle_new_user();

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Backfill: give any user who signed up before this migration a profile.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

insert into public.profiles (id, email, full_name)
select
  u.id,
  u.email,
  coalesce(
    nullif(u.raw_user_meta_data ->> 'full_name', ''),
    split_part(u.email, '@', 1)
  )
from auth.users u
on conflict (id) do nothing;

33	| `npm test` | Test runner (no test suite exists yet — see Limitations) |
34	| `npm run pretty` | Prettier over all JS/JSX/JSON |
35	
36	### Environment variables
37	
38	**You need to supply these — they are not in the repo and nothing is
39	hardcoded.** Copy `.env.example` to `.env.local` and fill in:
40	
41	| Variable | Where to get it | Required |
42	| --- | --- | --- |
43	| `REACT_APP_SUPABASE_URL` | Supabase dashboard → Project Settings → Data API → Project URL | Yes, for auth |
44	| `REACT_APP_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` | Same page → Project API keys → `anon` `public` | Yes, for auth |
45	
46	Notes:
47	
48	- Create React App only exposes variables prefixed with `REACT_APP_`, and it
49	  **inlines them at build time**. Restart `npm start` after editing
50	  `.env.local`; changing them requires a rebuild, not just a redeploy.
51	- The anon key is designed to be public and shipped in a browser bundle. It
52	  is not a secret. What actually protects your data is **Row Level Security**
53	  on every table — enable it before storing anything real.
54	- Never put the `service_role` key in this file or anywhere in the frontend.
55	- `.env.local` is gitignored. `.env.example` is committed and contains
56	  placeholders only.
57	
58	### Supabase project setup
59	
60	1. Create a project at [supabase.com](https://supabase.com).
61	2. **Authentication → Providers → Email**: enable it. Email/password is all
62	   this app uses; no OAuth provider is wired up.
63	3. **Authentication → URL Configuration**: set Site URL to
64	   `http://localhost:3000` for local development, and add your production
65	   origin to Redirect URLs before deploying. Confirmation and password-reset
66	   links point back to `/auth/sign-in` at whatever origin the user signed up
67	   from.
68	4. **Authentication → URL Configuration → Redirect URLs**: add
69	   `http://localhost:3000/**` (and `https://your-domain/**` for production).
70	   **This is required.** Every emailed link redirects to `/auth/callback`, and
71	   Supabase silently falls back to the Site URL if that path is not
72	   allow-listed — the link then appears to do nothing.
73	5. **Authentication → Email → Confirm email**: your call. Both are handled.
74	   - **On** (Supabase default): sign-up shows a "check your inbox" message
75	     with a resend option; the emailed link lands on `/auth/callback`, which
76	     establishes the session and forwards into the dashboard.
77	   - **Off**: sign-up returns a session immediately and goes straight to the
78	     dashboard.
79	6. **Run the database migration**: paste `supabase/migrations/0001_profiles.sql`
80	   into the SQL Editor and run it. It creates `public.profiles`, enables RLS
81	   with owner-only policies, and adds a trigger that creates a profile row on
82	   signup. Without it the app still works, but the profile page falls back to
83	   session data and the console warns.
84	7. Supabase's built-in SMTP is heavily rate-limited (a few messages per hour)
85	   and intended only for testing. Configure your own SMTP before any real
86	   signup volume.
87	
88	If the two env vars are missing the app still builds and runs — the landing
89	page works, and the auth screens render with an explanatory banner and
90	disabled submit buttons rather than crashing.

92	---
93	
94	## Tech stack
95	
96	| Layer | Choice | Why |
97	| --- | --- | --- |
98	| UI | React 19 | Already the base of the template this product is derived from; no reason to churn it. |
99	| Build | Create React App (`react-scripts` 5) | Inherited. Kept deliberately — see Limitations. |
100	| Routing | React Router 6 | Inherited; `ProtectedRoute` composes cleanly with its element API. |
101	| Styling | Tailwind CSS 3 | Inherited, and the brand kit maps onto a token-based utility system almost directly. |
102	| Charts | ApexCharts via `react-apexcharts` | Inherited. Colors now come from the brand kit's `dataviz-categorical` palette. |
103	| Auth | Supabase Auth (`@supabase/supabase-js` v2) | Requested. Hosted email/password with session persistence and refresh handled for us — no backend to run. |
104	| Icons | `react-icons` | Inherited. |

125	### Design tokens
126	
127	`tailwind.config.js` is the single source of truth for color. It reads from
128	the brand kit anchors and exposes:
129	
130	- `primary-*` (indigo, `500` = `#4F46E5`), also aliased as `brand-*`
131	- `accent-*` (spark cyan, `500` = `#22D3EE`)
132	- `neutral-*` (Nova gray ramp), also aliased as `gray-*`

content.text:
**Heads up first:** the values landed in `.env.example`, which is **tracked by git**. I moved them to `.env.local` (gitignored) and restored the placeholders. They were never committed, so nothing is in history. I also stripped `/rest/v1/` from the URL — `supabase-js` needs the bare project URL and appends the paths itself.

## Verified against your live project

- Auth endpoint reachable, key accepted, email provider on, signups enabled
- A real sign-in attempt returns a live Supabase response, correctly mapped to *"That email and password don't match an account."*
- `mailer_autoconfirm: false` → **email confirmation is ON**
- **Zero tables exposed** — the DB is empty, which is why the dashboard stays on fixtures

## What I built

**`supabase/migrations/0001_profiles.sql`** — `public.profiles` keyed to `auth.users`, RLS with owner-only policies, and an on-signup trigger seeding the row (plus a backfill). `SECURITY DEFINER` with empty `search_path` and fully-qualified names, per Supabase's hardening guidance.

**Email confirmation now actually lands somewhere.** It previously redirected to `/auth/sign-in`, which established a session *behind a login form the user no longer needed* — the link read as if it had done nothing. New `/auth/callback` consumes the token fragment and forwards signups into the dashboard, recovery links to a new `/auth/reset-password` screen, and gives expired/used links a real explanation. Verified the expired-link path renders correctly.

Also: optional full-name field at signup (feeds the trigger), a resend-confirmation button, and the profile page + navbar now read the real account instead of the hardcoded sample user.

The app degrades gracefully if the migration hasn't run — it warns and falls back to session data rather than breaking.

## Two things only you can do

**1. Run the migration** — Supabase → SQL Editor → New query → paste `supabase/migrations/0001_profiles.sql` → Run.

I deliberately didn't ask for your `service_role` key or DB password to run this myself; DDL via a pasted migration is the right path.

**2. Allow-list the callback** — Authentication → URL Configuration → Redirect URLs → add:

```
http://localhost:3000/**
```

**This one is not optional.** Supabase silently drops any `emailRedirectTo` path that isn't allow-listed and falls back to the Site URL, so without it the confirmation link will appear to do nothing — the exact failure I just fixed.

## Then

Dev server is still up on `localhost:3000`. Once those two are done, tell me and I'll run a real signup end to end. I'll need to know which address to use — I'd rather not send a confirmation email to an inbox I can't reach, and your built-in SMTP only allows a few sends per hour, so a wasted one costs real waiting time. Your own address works if you're willing to click the link.

Clean — the only matches are my own comments and an `email` column reference. No credentials, no data, no project identifiers.

**Why it should stay committed:**

- It's the only record of your schema outside the dashboard. Gitignored, `public.profiles` exists solely as something someone clicked once, with no history of who changed what or why.
- The app depends on it. `AuthContext` queries `profiles`, and the signup trigger is what creates the row. A fresh clone with the migration ignored gives you an app that silently warns and degrades.
- Reproducibility — staging, a second dev, a rebuild after an incident all need to recreate this exactly.
- It's DDL, not data. No rows, no keys, no PII.

The instinct is right in general, just aimed at the wrong file — `.env.example` was genuinely the risky one, and that's now handled.

**What *does* need ignoring** is the Supabase CLI's local artifacts, if you ever run `supabase init`/`supabase start`. Those don't exist yet, but `config.toml` in particular can end up holding SMTP passwords and OAuth secrets. Adding the entries now so they can't bite later:

# Nova Analytics — functional dashboard + Supabase backend + Vercel

## Context

The whitelabel is done: branding, theme, landing page, and working Supabase
email/password auth with a `profiles` table. But the dashboard is still a
shell — every KPI, chart and table reads a JSON fixture from
`src/views/admin/*/variables/`. The only live data in the app is the
signed-in user.

This plan makes the dashboard real and ships it on Vercel. Three decisions
are locked in from discussion:

- **Data origin — phased.** Phase A makes every entity a real, editable
  Supabase row with metric history from a seed script. Phase B adds the
  public ingest endpoint. The schema is designed up front to accept real
  events so Phase B is additive, not a rewrite.
- **Tenancy — workspaces with members.** Matches the "invite everyone,
  priced on volume" story already on the pricing page, and avoids rewriting
  every RLS policy later.
- **Build — migrate to Vite first.** CRA is deprecated and the backend adds
  more env vars; migrating first renames them once instead of twice.

Outcome: a deployed app where signing up creates a workspace, and every
number on the dashboard comes from Postgres.

---

## Phase 0 — Migrate CRA → Vite

Small and fully mapped. Do it first and in isolation so it's easy to review.

- Add `vite`, `@vitejs/plugin-react`; drop `react-scripts`. Scripts become
  `vite` / `vite build` / `vite preview`.
- New `vite.config.js`: React plugin, `resolve.alias` for the `src`-rooted
  absolute imports that `jsconfig.json` currently provides (`baseUrl: "src"`),
  and `server.port: 3000` to keep the Supabase redirect allow-list valid.
- Move `public/index.html` → repo root; strip the four `%PUBLIC_URL%` prefixes
  (Vite serves `public/` at `/`).
- **Rename the two `.js` files containing JSX** — Vite will not transform JSX
  in `.js`: `src/index.js` → `index.jsx`, `src/routes.js` → `routes.jsx`.
  Then fix the three explicit specifiers `import routes from "routes.js"` in
  `src/components/sidebar/index.jsx`, `src/layouts/admin/index.jsx`,
  `src/layouts/auth/index.jsx` → `"routes"`. `variables/charts.js` and both
  `columnsData.js` are plain JS and stay.
- Env rename: `REACT_APP_*` → `VITE_*`, `process.env` → `import.meta.env`.
  Only `src/lib/supabase.js` reads them (2 lines). Update `.env.example`,
  `.env.local`, and the README env table.

## Phase 1 — Deploy to Vercel

Ship the static app before the backend exists, so env/redirect problems
surface while the surface area is small.

- `vercel.json`: SPA rewrite (`/(.*)` → `/index.html`) — without it every
  deep link 404s. Plus baseline security headers.
- Vercel project env vars: `VITE_SUPABASE_URL`, `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`.
  These are inlined at build time, so changing them needs a redeploy.
- **Supabase → Authentication → URL Configuration**: set Site URL to the
  production domain and add both `https://<prod-domain>/**` and the preview
  wildcard `https://<project>-*-<team>.vercel.app/**`. Preview deploys get
  unique URLs; without the wildcard, auth emails from a preview branch
  redirect to production.

## Phase 2 — Backend schema

Migrations in `supabase/migrations/`, run via the SQL Editor as with
`0001_profiles.sql`. Follow that file's conventions: RLS on every table,
`SECURITY DEFINER` functions with `set search_path = ''` and fully-qualified
names.

**`0002_workspaces.sql`** — tenancy
- `workspaces` (name, slug, plan, data_residency)
- `workspace_members` (workspace_id, user_id, role) — PK on the pair
- `workspace_invites` (email, role, token, expires_at, accepted_at)
- `profiles.default_workspace_id` added
- **`is_workspace_member(uuid)` / `is_workspace_admin(uuid)`** as
  `SECURITY DEFINER` helpers. Critical: an RLS policy on `workspace_members`
  that itself queries `workspace_members` causes infinite recursion — every
  policy must go through these helpers.
- Extend the existing `handle_new_user` trigger: on signup, also create a
  personal workspace, add the user as `owner`, and set
  `default_workspace_id`. Backfill for existing users.

**`0003_domain.sql`** — the entities behind the tables and lists
- `data_sources` (name, kind, status, platforms text[], last_sync_at,
  health_pct, write_key_hash) → backs CheckTable, DevelopmentTable,
  ColumnsTable, and the "Data Sources" KPI
- `reports` (name, status, schedule, last_run_at, progress) → ComplexTable
- `alerts` (metric_key, comparator, threshold, is_active, triggered_at) →
  "Active Alerts" KPI + navbar notifications
- `tasks` (title, is_done, position) → TaskCard
- `notifications` (title, body, kind, read_at) → navbar dropdown
- All keyed to `workspace_id`, all RLS'd via `is_workspace_member`.

**`0004_metrics.sql`** — one flexible table behind all charts and KPIs
```
metric_points (workspace_id, bucket timestamptz, grain, metric_key,
               dims jsonb, value numeric)
```
Unique on `(workspace_id, bucket, grain, metric_key, dims)`, GIN on `dims`.
One table serves all four charts rather than a bespoke table each:
- line chart → `metric_key='revenue'|'profit'`, `grain='month'`
- stacked bar → `metric_key='revenue'`, `dims->>'stream'`, `grain='day'`
- daily traffic → `metric_key='visitors'`, `grain='hour'`
- pie → `metric_key='sessions'`, `dims->>'platform'`

Also `events` (workspace_id, data_source_id, name, occurred_at, distinct_id,
platform, properties jsonb, revenue_cents) — created now, populated in
Phase 5.

**`0005_rpc.sql`** — `get_dashboard_kpis(workspace_id, range)` returning the
six KPIs plus period-over-period deltas in one row. Six separate queries for
one card row is the obvious thing to get wrong.

**`0006_seed.sql`** — idempotent demo seed: ~6 data sources, 4 reports, a few
alerts and tasks, and 90 days of `metric_points` with plausible trend and
weekly seasonality. This is what makes the dashboard look alive before
ingestion exists.

## Phase 3 — Frontend data layer

- Add `@tanstack/react-query` (`@tanstack/react-table` is already a dep, so
  this is consistent). `QueryClientProvider` in `src/App.jsx` inside
  `AuthProvider`.
- **`src/contexts/WorkspaceContext.jsx`** — resolves the active workspace
  from `profiles.default_workspace_id`, falling back to first membership.
  Mirror the structure of `src/contexts/AuthContext.jsx` (same
  loading/`isConfigured` shape, same graceful degradation when a table is
  missing).
- **`src/lib/queries/`** — one module per entity (`dataSources.js`,
  `reports.js`, `metrics.js`, `tasks.js`, `alerts.js`), each exporting typed
  hooks. Every query filters by `workspace_id`; RLS is the enforcement, the
  filter is for index use.
- Shared loading/empty/error states. Reuse
  `src/views/auth/components/AuthFeedback.jsx` for errors and the
  `NovaLogo animate-pulse` idiom from
  `src/components/auth/ProtectedRoute.jsx` for loading.

## Phase 4 — Wire the dashboard

- **Table components need no changes** — `CheckTable`, `ComplexTable`,
  `ColumnsTable`, `DevelopmentTable` already take a `tableData` prop. Only
  the parent views (`src/views/admin/default/index.jsx`,
  `src/views/admin/tables/index.jsx`) change: fetch, map to the existing row
  shape, pass down. Note `CheckTable` expects `name` as a
  `[label, boolean]` tuple.
- **Chart components must be refactored to accept props.** `TotalSpent`,
  `WeeklyRevenue`, `DailyTraffic` and `PieChartCard` currently import their
  series directly from `src/variables/charts.js`. Keep the *options* exports
  there (they carry the brand palette and mono fonts); delete the *data*
  exports.
- KPI widget row driven by `get_dashboard_kpis`, with real deltas replacing
  the hardcoded `+2.45%`.
- `TaskCard` becomes interactive — checkbox toggles persist to `tasks`.
- Navbar notifications read `notifications`; mark-all-read writes back.
- Profile page: back the remaining hardcoded cards (Plan, Data residency)
  with `workspaces` columns, and make `Storage`/`Project` read real counts.

## Phase 5 — Ingestion (the "real product" step)

- Edge Function `supabase/functions/ingest/index.ts`: accepts a per-source
  write key, validates against `data_sources.write_key_hash`, inserts into
  `events`. Write key shown once at creation, stored hashed.
- `pg_cron` job calling a `refresh_metric_points()` aggregate that rolls
  `events` into `metric_points` — same table the seed writes to, so the UI
  needs no changes when real data starts arriving.
- UI to create a data source and reveal its write key once.

---

## Verification

Per phase, not just at the end:

- **Phase 0**: `npm run build` clean; `npm run preview`; walk landing →
  sign-in → dashboard in the browser and confirm no console errors and no
  broken asset/icon paths (the `%PUBLIC_URL%` and JSX-rename changes are
  exactly what would break here).
- **Phase 1**: hit the deployed URL, hard-refresh on `/auth/sign-in` to prove
  the SPA rewrite works, and complete one real signup from the deployed
  origin to prove the redirect allow-list is right.
- **Phase 2**: run each migration in the SQL Editor. Then verify RLS actually
  isolates: sign in as two users in separate browser profiles and confirm
  neither sees the other's workspace rows. A table with RLS enabled but no
  policy returns empty rather than erroring — check for rows, not just
  absence of errors.
- **Phase 3/4**: drive the dashboard with Chrome MCP; confirm each KPI and
  chart matches a `select` run against the same data in the SQL Editor.
  Check loading and empty states by signing in as a brand-new user with an
  unseeded workspace.
- **Phase 5**: `curl` the ingest endpoint with a valid and an invalid write
  key; confirm the row lands in `events`, run the rollup, confirm the chart
  moves.

## Risks and open items

- **RLS recursion** on `workspace_members` is the single most likely bug.
  The `is_workspace_member` helper exists specifically to avoid it.
- **Vite JSX rename** is the most likely Phase 0 breakage — `routes.js` is
  imported by explicit filename in three places.
- **Vercel preview URLs** silently break auth redirects without the wildcard
  entry.
- **Landing page copy is still fiction** — pricing tiers, "99.98% uptime",
  "SOC 2 Type II". Once `workspaces.plan` exists the tiers should either
  become real or be softened. The compliance claim should not ship
  unreviewed.
- **Still no tests.** Worth adding coverage on the RLS policies and the KPI
  RPC at minimum, since those are where a silent bug leaks data.

toolUseResult.plan:
# Nova Analytics — functional dashboard + Supabase backend + Vercel

## Context

The whitelabel is done: branding, theme, landing page, and working Supabase
email/password auth with a `profiles` table. But the dashboard is still a
shell — every KPI, chart and table reads a JSON fixture from
`src/views/admin/*/variables/`. The only live data in the app is the
signed-in user.

This plan makes the dashboard real and ships it on Vercel. Three decisions
are locked in from discussion:

- **Data origin — phased.** Phase A makes every entity a real, editable
  Supabase row with metric history from a seed script. Phase B adds the
  public ingest endpoint. The schema is designed up front to accept real
  events so Phase B is additive, not a rewrite.
- **Tenancy — workspaces with members.** Matches the "invite everyone,
  priced on volume" story already on the pricing page, and avoids rewriting
  every RLS policy later.
- **Build — migrate to Vite first.** CRA is deprecated and the backend adds
  more env vars; migrating first renames them once instead of twice.

Outcome: a deployed app where signing up creates a workspace, and every
number on the dashboard comes from Postgres.

---

## Phase 0 — Migrate CRA → Vite

Small and fully mapped. Do it first and in isolation so it's easy to review.

- Add `vite`, `@vitejs/plugin-react`; drop `react-scripts`. Scripts become
  `vite` / `vite build` / `vite preview`.
- New `vite.config.js`: React plugin, `resolve.alias` for the `src`-rooted
  absolute imports that `jsconfig.json` currently provides (`baseUrl: "src"`),
  and `server.port: 3000` to keep the Supabase redirect allow-list valid.
- Move `public/index.html` → repo root; strip the four `%PUBLIC_URL%` prefixes
  (Vite serves `public/` at `/`).
- **Rename the two `.js` files containing JSX** — Vite will not transform JSX
  in `.js`: `src/index.js` → `index.jsx`, `src/routes.js` → `routes.jsx`.
  Then fix the three explicit specifiers `import routes from "routes.js"` in
  `src/components/sidebar/index.jsx`, `src/layouts/admin/index.jsx`,
  `src/layouts/auth/index.jsx` → `"routes"`. `variables/charts.js` and both
  `columnsData.js` are plain JS and stay.
- Env rename: `REACT_APP_*` → `VITE_*`, `process.env` → `import.meta.env`.
  Only `src/lib/supabase.js` reads them (2 lines). Update `.env.example`,
  `.env.local`, and the README env table.

## Phase 1 — Deploy to Vercel

Ship the static app before the backend exists, so env/redirect problems
surface while the surface area is small.

- `vercel.json`: SPA rewrite (`/(.*)` → `/index.html`) — without it every
  deep link 404s. Plus baseline security headers.
- Vercel project env vars: `VITE_SUPABASE_URL`, `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`.
  These are inlined at build time, so changing them needs a redeploy.
- **Supabase → Authentication → URL Configuration**: set Site URL to the
  production domain and add both `https://<prod-domain>/**` and the preview
  wildcard `https://<project>-*-<team>.vercel.app/**`. Preview deploys get
  unique URLs; without the wildcard, auth emails from a preview branch
  redirect to production.

## Phase 2 — Backend schema

Migrations in `supabase/migrations/`, run via the SQL Editor as with
`0001_profiles.sql`. Follow that file's conventions: RLS on every table,
`SECURITY DEFINER` functions with `set search_path = ''` and fully-qualified
names.

**`0002_workspaces.sql`** — tenancy
- `workspaces` (name, slug, plan, data_residency)
- `workspace_members` (workspace_id, user_id, role) — PK on the pair
- `workspace_invites` (email, role, token, expires_at, accepted_at)
- `profiles.default_workspace_id` added
- **`is_workspace_member(uuid)` / `is_workspace_admin(uuid)`** as
  `SECURITY DEFINER` helpers. Critical: an RLS policy on `workspace_members`
  that itself queries `workspace_members` causes infinite recursion — every
  policy must go through these helpers.
- Extend the existing `handle_new_user` trigger: on signup, also create a
  personal workspace, add the user as `owner`, and set
  `default_workspace_id`. Backfill for existing users.

**`0003_domain.sql`** — the entities behind the tables and lists
- `data_sources` (name, kind, status, platforms text[], last_sync_at,
  health_pct, write_key_hash) → backs CheckTable, DevelopmentTable,
  ColumnsTable, and the "Data Sources" KPI
- `reports` (name, status, schedule, last_run_at, progress) → ComplexTable
- `alerts` (metric_key, comparator, threshold, is_active, triggered_at) →
  "Active Alerts" KPI + navbar notifications
- `tasks` (title, is_done, position) → TaskCard
- `notifications` (title, body, kind, read_at) → navbar dropdown
- All keyed to `workspace_id`, all RLS'd via `is_workspace_member`.

**`0004_metrics.sql`** — one flexible table behind all charts and KPIs
```
metric_points (workspace_id, bucket timestamptz, grain, metric_key,
               dims jsonb, value numeric)
```
Unique on `(workspace_id, bucket, grain, metric_key, dims)`, GIN on `dims`.
One table serves all four charts rather than a bespoke table each:
- line chart → `metric_key='revenue'|'profit'`, `grain='month'`
- stacked bar → `metric_key='revenue'`, `dims->>'stream'`, `grain='day'`
- daily traffic → `metric_key='visitors'`, `grain='hour'`
- pie → `metric_key='sessions'`, `dims->>'platform'`

Also `events` (workspace_id, data_source_id, name, occurred_at, distinct_id,
platform, properties jsonb, revenue_cents) — created now, populated in
Phase 5.

**`0005_rpc.sql`** — `get_dashboard_kpis(workspace_id, range)` returning the
six KPIs plus period-over-period deltas in one row. Six separate queries for
one card row is the obvious thing to get wrong.

**`0006_seed.sql`** — idempotent demo seed: ~6 data sources, 4 reports, a few
alerts and tasks, and 90 days of `metric_points` with plausible trend and
weekly seasonality. This is what makes the dashboard look alive before
ingestion exists.

## Phase 3 — Frontend data layer

- Add `@tanstack/react-query` (`@tanstack/react-table` is already a dep, so
  this is consistent). `QueryClientProvider` in `src/App.jsx` inside
  `AuthProvider`.
- **`src/contexts/WorkspaceContext.jsx`** — resolves the active workspace
  from `profiles.default_workspace_id`, falling back to first membership.
  Mirror the structure of `src/contexts/AuthContext.jsx` (same
  loading/`isConfigured` shape, same graceful degradation when a table is
  missing).
- **`src/lib/queries/`** — one module per entity (`dataSources.js`,
  `reports.js`, `metrics.js`, `tasks.js`, `alerts.js`), each exporting typed
  hooks. Every query filters by `workspace_id`; RLS is the enforcement, the
  filter is for index use.
- Shared loading/empty/error states. Reuse
  `src/views/auth/components/AuthFeedback.jsx` for errors and the
  `NovaLogo animate-pulse` idiom from
  `src/components/auth/ProtectedRoute.jsx` for loading.

## Phase 4 — Wire the dashboard

- **Table components need no changes** — `CheckTable`, `ComplexTable`,
  `ColumnsTable`, `DevelopmentTable` already take a `tableData` prop. Only
  the parent views (`src/views/admin/default/index.jsx`,
  `src/views/admin/tables/index.jsx`) change: fetch, map to the existing row
  shape, pass down. Note `CheckTable` expects `name` as a
  `[label, boolean]` tuple.
- **Chart components must be refactored to accept props.** `TotalSpent`,
  `WeeklyRevenue`, `DailyTraffic` and `PieChartCard` currently import their
  series directly from `src/variables/charts.js`. Keep the *options* exports
  there (they carry the brand palette and mono fonts); delete the *data*
  exports.
- KPI widget row driven by `get_dashboard_kpis`, with real deltas replacing
  the hardcoded `+2.45%`.
- `TaskCard` becomes interactive — checkbox toggles persist to `tasks`.
- Navbar notifications read `notifications`; mark-all-read writes back.
- Profile page: back the remaining hardcoded cards (Plan, Data residency)
  with `workspaces` columns, and make `Storage`/`Project` read real counts.

## Phase 5 — Ingestion (the "real product" step)

- Edge Function `supabase/functions/ingest/index.ts`: accepts a per-source
  write key, validates against `data_sources.write_key_hash`, inserts into
  `events`. Write key shown once at creation, stored hashed.
- `pg_cron` job calling a `refresh_metric_points()` aggregate that rolls
  `events` into `metric_points` — same table the seed writes to, so the UI
  needs no changes when real data starts arriving.
- UI to create a data source and reveal its write key once.

---

## Verification

Per phase, not just at the end:

- **Phase 0**: `npm run build` clean; `npm run preview`; walk landing →
  sign-in → dashboard in the browser and confirm no console errors and no
  broken asset/icon paths (the `%PUBLIC_URL%` and JSX-rename changes are
  exactly what would break here).
- **Phase 1**: hit the deployed URL, hard-refresh on `/auth/sign-in` to prove
  the SPA rewrite works, and complete one real signup from the deployed
  origin to prove the redirect allow-list is right.
- **Phase 2**: run each migration in the SQL Editor. Then verify RLS actually
  isolates: sign in as two users in separate browser profiles and confirm
  neither sees the other's workspace rows. A table with RLS enabled but no
  policy returns empty rather than erroring — check for rows, not just
  absence of errors.
- **Phase 3/4**: drive the dashboard with Chrome MCP; confirm each KPI and
  chart matches a `select` run against the same data in the SQL Editor.
  Check loading and empty states by signing in as a brand-new user with an
  unseeded workspace.
- **Phase 5**: `curl` the ingest endpoint with a valid and an invalid write
  key; confirm the row lands in `events`, run the rollup, confirm the chart
  moves.

## Risks and open items

- **RLS recursion** on `workspace_members` is the single most likely bug.
  The `is_workspace_member` helper exists specifically to avoid it.
- **Vite JSX rename** is the most likely Phase 0 breakage — `routes.js` is
  imported by explicit filename in three places.
- **Vercel preview URLs** silently break auth redirects without the wildcard
  entry.
- **Landing page copy is still fiction** — pricing tiers, "99.98% uptime",
  "SOC 2 Type II". Once `workspaces.plan` exists the tiers should either
  become real or be softened. The compliance claim should not ship
  unreviewed.
- **Still no tests.** Worth adding coverage on the RLS policies and the KPI
  RPC at minimum, since those are where a silent bug leaks data.

## Deployment (Vercel)

`npm run build` emits a static bundle in `dist/`. `vercel.json` is committed
and configures the deploy; Vercel needs no dashboard build settings.

**What `vercel.json` does, and why:**

- **SPA fallback** — rewrites everything to `/index.html`. Without it,
  hard-refreshing `/auth/sign-in` (or opening any emailed auth link) returns
  404, because no such file exists. Vercel checks the filesystem *before*
  rewrites, so real assets, `favicon.ico` and `manifest.json` still win over
  the catch-all.
- **Immutable caching** on `/assets/*`, which Vite content-hashes.
- **Baseline security headers** — nosniff, `DENY` framing, a conservative
  referrer policy, HSTS.

Note `vercel.json` has no comments because JSON has none, and Vercel
validates the file strictly — adding an unrecognised key (including a
`comment` key) fails the build rather than being ignored.

### Steps

1. Import the repo in Vercel. It will detect Vite; `vercel.json` pins the
   build command and output directory regardless.
2. **Project → Settings → Environment Variables**, for Production, Preview
   *and* Development:
   - `VITE_SUPABASE_URL`
   - `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`

   These are inlined into the bundle at build time, so changing one requires
   a **redeploy**, not just a restart.
3. **Supabase → Authentication → URL Configuration**:
   - Site URL: your production origin, e.g. `https://nova-analytics.vercel.app`
   - Redirect URLs — add **both**:
     ```
     https://<your-production-domain>/**
     https://<project>-*-<your-team>.vercel.app/**
     ```
     The second entry matters: every preview deployment gets a unique
     generated hostname. Without the wildcard, a signup from a preview branch
     sends a confirmation link that redirects to production, where the token
     is not valid for that origin — the link appears to silently fail.

### Not yet configured

A **Content-Security-Policy** is deliberately absent. The correct policy for
this app needs `connect-src` for `https://*.supabase.co`, font origins for
`fonts.googleapis.com` / `fonts.gstatic.com`, and `style-src 'unsafe-inline'`
for the styles Tailwind and ApexCharts inject at runtime. Shipping an
untested CSP breaks the app in ways that are hard to diagnose, so it should
be added and verified against a preview deployment rather than guessed at
here.

# Nova Analytics

The Nova Analytics web app: a marketing landing page, email/password
authentication, and a whitelabeled analytics dashboard.

```
/                    Landing page (public)
/auth/sign-in        Sign in
/auth/sign-up        Create account
/admin/*             Dashboard — requires an authenticated session
```

---

## Setup

Requires **Node.js 18+** (LTS recommended) and npm.

```bash
git clone <this-repo>
cd nova-analytics-dashboard
npm install
cp .env.example .env.local     # then fill in the values — see below
npm start                      # http://localhost:3000
```

Other scripts:

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run dev` (or `npm start`) | Vite dev server on port 3000 |
| `npm run build` | Production bundle into `dist/` |
| `npm run preview` | Serve the production build locally on port 3000 |
| `npm run pretty` | Prettier over `src/**/*.{js,jsx,json}` |

There is no test script — no test runner is configured yet. See Limitations.

### Environment variables

**You need to supply these — they are not in the repo and nothing is
hardcoded.** Copy `.env.example` to `.env.local` and fill in:

| Variable | Where to get it | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `VITE_SUPABASE_URL` | Supabase dashboard → Project Settings → Data API → Project URL | Yes, for auth |
| `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` | Same page → Project API keys → `anon` `public` | Yes, for auth |

Notes:

- Vite only exposes variables prefixed with `VITE_`, and it **inlines them at
  build time**. Restart the dev server after editing
  `.env.local`; changing them requires a rebuild, not just a redeploy.
- The anon key is designed to be public and shipped in a browser bundle. It
  is not a secret. What actually protects your data is **Row Level Security**
  on every table — enable it before storing anything real.
- Never put the `service_role` key in this file or anywhere in the frontend.
- `.env.local` is gitignored. `.env.example` is committed and contains
  placeholders only.

### Supabase project setup

1. Create a project at [supabase.com](https://supabase.com).
2. **Authentication → Providers → Email**: enable it. Email/password is all
   this app uses; no OAuth provider is wired up.
3. **Authentication → URL Configuration → Site URL**: `http://localhost:3000`
   for local development; your real origin before deploying.
4. **Authentication → URL Configuration → Redirect URLs**: add
   `http://localhost:3000/**` (and `https://your-domain/**` for production).
   **This is required.** Every emailed link redirects to `/auth/callback`, and
   Supabase silently falls back to the Site URL if that path is not
   allow-listed — the link then appears to do nothing.
5. **Authentication → Email → Confirm email**: your call. Both are handled.
   - **On** (Supabase default): sign-up shows a "check your inbox" message
     with a resend option; the emailed link lands on `/auth/callback`, which
     establishes the session and forwards into the dashboard.
   - **Off**: sign-up returns a session immediately and goes straight to the
     dashboard.
6. **Run the database migration**: paste `supabase/migrations/0001_profiles.sql`
   into the SQL Editor and run it. It creates `public.profiles`, enables RLS
   with owner-only policies, and adds a trigger that creates a profile row on
   signup. Without it the app still works, but the profile page falls back to
   session data and the console warns.
7. Supabase's built-in SMTP is heavily rate-limited (a few messages per hour)
   and intended only for testing. Configure your own SMTP before any real
   signup volume.

If the two env vars are missing the app still builds and runs — the landing
page works, and the auth screens render with an explanatory banner and
disabled submit buttons rather than crashing.

---

## Tech stack

| Layer | Choice | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| UI | React 19 | Already the base of the template this product is derived from; no reason to churn it. |
| Build | Vite 8 | Migrated off the inherited Create React App, which is deprecated and carried transitive CVEs. Build went from ~40s to ~0.6s, and route-level code splitting became straightforward. |
| Routing | React Router 6 | Inherited; `ProtectedRoute` composes cleanly with its element API. |
| Styling | Tailwind CSS 3 | Inherited, and the brand kit maps onto a token-based utility system almost directly. |
| Charts | ApexCharts via `react-apexcharts` | Inherited. Colors now come from the brand kit's `dataviz-categorical` palette. |
| Auth | Supabase Auth (`@supabase/supabase-js` v2) | Requested. Hosted email/password with session persistence and refresh handled for us — no backend to run. |
| Icons | `react-icons` | Inherited. |

### Where things live

```
nova_analytics_id/        Brand kit — logos, color/type tokens, guidelines
src/
  assets/img/layout/nova/ Nova logo SVGs + favicon source
  components/
    auth/ProtectedRoute   Session gate for /admin/*
    brand/NovaLogo        Inline-SVG logo (mark | horizontal | stacked)
  contexts/AuthContext    Session + profile state, all auth actions
  lib/supabase.js         Supabase client, reads env vars
  views/
    landing/              Marketing page and its sections
    auth/                 SignIn, SignUp, AuthCallback, ResetPassword
    admin/                Dashboard, data tables, profile
  routes.js               Sidebar + router route table
supabase/migrations/      SQL to run in the Supabase SQL Editor
tailwind.config.js        Nova design tokens
```

### Design tokens

`tailwind.config.js` is the single source of truth for color. It reads from
the brand kit anchors and exposes:

- `primary-*` (indigo, `500` = `#4F46E5`), also aliased as `brand-*`
- `accent-*` (spark cyan, `500` = `#22D3EE`)
- `neutral-*` (Nova gray ramp), also aliased as `gray-*`
- `amber-*` (secondary accent), `success` / `warning` / `danger` / `info`
- `navy-*` — the dark-mode surface ramp, running ink → indigo-darker

Fonts: `font-display` (Space Grotesk), `font-sans` (Inter, the default), and
`font-mono` (JetBrains Mono, used for metrics, tables and code). Loaded from
Google Fonts in `src/index.css`, which also re-exports every token as a CSS
custom property (`--nova-indigo`, `--nova-font-body`, …).

The brand kit specifies anchor values, not full ramps. Intermediate steps
(`primary` 50–400, `neutral` 200/400/600/800, `accent` 600–900) are
interpolated in `tailwind.config.js` and marked as such in comments.

---

## Known limitations and shortcuts

Things worth knowing before this goes in front of anyone:

**Auth**

- Email/password only. No OAuth, no magic links, no MFA. The
  non-functional "Sign in with Google" button from the template was removed
  rather than left as decoration.
- Password reset is complete: request → email → `/auth/callback` →
  `/auth/reset-password` → signed in with the new password.
- `public.profiles` stores name, role and team, and the navbar/profile page
  read from it. Nothing in the UI edits it yet — role and team are set
  directly in the database.
