-- Nova Analytics — 0004_metrics
--
-- Two tables: raw `events` (populated in phase 5 by the ingest function) and
-- `metric_points`, the rolled-up series everything on screen actually reads.
--
-- metric_points is deliberately one generic table rather than a bespoke table
-- per chart. Each chart is a different slice of the same shape:
--
--   TotalSpent line     -> metric_key in ('revenue','profit'), grain 'month'
--   WeeklyRevenue bars  -> metric_key 'revenue', grain 'day',
--                          dims->>'stream' in (subscriptions|usage|services)
--   DailyTraffic bars   -> metric_key 'visitors', grain 'hour'
--   Traffic pie         -> metric_key 'sessions', grain 'day',
--                          dims->>'platform' in (web|mobile|api)
--
-- Adding a chart means adding rows, not a migration.

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- events — raw, append-only
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create table if not exists public.events (
  id             bigint      generated always as identity primary key,
  workspace_id   uuid        not null references public.workspaces (id) on delete cascade,
  data_source_id uuid        references public.data_sources (id) on delete set null,
  name           text        not null,
  occurred_at    timestamptz not null default now(),
  -- Anonymous or identified actor; what "active users" counts distinctly.
  distinct_id    text,
  platform       text        check (platform in ('web', 'mobile', 'api', 'server')),
  properties     jsonb       not null default '{}'::jsonb,
  revenue_cents  bigint      not null default 0,
  created_at     timestamptz not null default now()
);

create index if not exists events_workspace_occurred_idx
  on public.events (workspace_id, occurred_at desc);
create index if not exists events_workspace_name_idx
  on public.events (workspace_id, name, occurred_at desc);
create index if not exists events_properties_idx
  on public.events using gin (properties);

alter table public.events enable row level security;

-- Read-only from the browser. Writes arrive through the ingest edge function
-- (phase 5), which authenticates a per-source write key rather than a user.
drop policy if exists "Members read events" on public.events;
create policy "Members read events"
  on public.events for select
  using (public.is_workspace_member(workspace_id));

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- metric_points — the aggregated series behind every chart and KPI
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create table if not exists public.metric_points (
  workspace_id uuid        not null references public.workspaces (id) on delete cascade,
  bucket       timestamptz not null,
  grain        text        not null check (grain in ('hour', 'day', 'month')),
  metric_key   text        not null,
  dims         jsonb       not null default '{}'::jsonb,
  value        numeric     not null default 0,
  updated_at   timestamptz not null default now(),
  -- One row per series point. The rollup upserts on this, so re-running it is
  -- idempotent. dims participates in the key so a metric can be sliced by
  -- platform or revenue stream without colliding.
  primary key (workspace_id, grain, metric_key, bucket, dims)
);

create index if not exists metric_points_lookup_idx
  on public.metric_points (workspace_id, metric_key, grain, bucket desc);
create index if not exists metric_points_dims_idx
  on public.metric_points using gin (dims);

alter table public.metric_points enable row level security;

drop policy if exists "Members read metrics" on public.metric_points;
create policy "Members read metrics"
  on public.metric_points for select
  using (public.is_workspace_member(workspace_id));

-- Seeding and the phase-5 rollup both run as definer functions, so no write
-- policy is exposed to the browser.

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Series reader
--
-- One RPC for every chart. Returning the slice pre-shaped keeps the client
-- from pulling a wide range and filtering in JS.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create or replace function public.get_metric_series(
  target_workspace uuid,
  metric           text,
  series_grain     text,
  since            timestamptz default null,
  dim_key          text        default null
)
returns table (bucket timestamptz, dim_value text, value numeric)
language sql
stable
security invoker
set search_path = ''
as $$
  select
    p.bucket,
    case when dim_key is null then null else p.dims ->> dim_key end as dim_value,
    sum(p.value) as value
  from public.metric_points p
  where p.workspace_id = target_workspace
    and p.metric_key   = metric
    and p.grain        = series_grain
    and (since is null or p.bucket >= since)
  group by p.bucket, 2
  order by p.bucket;
$$;

-- SECURITY INVOKER above is deliberate: the caller's RLS on metric_points
-- still applies, so this cannot be used to read another tenant's series.

revoke execute on function public.get_metric_series(uuid, text, text, timestamptz, text) from public;
grant execute on function public.get_metric_series(uuid, text, text, timestamptz, text) to authenticated;

-- Nova Analytics — 0005_rpc
--
-- get_dashboard_kpis: the six-tile row at the top of the dashboard, plus
-- period-over-period deltas, in one round trip.
--
-- Six separate queries for one card row is the obvious thing to get wrong —
-- it is also six chances for the tiles to disagree with each other if data
-- changes mid-render. One call, one snapshot.

create or replace function public.get_dashboard_kpis(
  target_workspace uuid,
  window_days      integer default 30
)
returns table (
  monthly_revenue        numeric,
  monthly_revenue_delta  numeric,
  active_users           numeric,
  active_users_delta     numeric,
  events_tracked         numeric,
  events_tracked_delta   numeric,
  conversion_rate        numeric,
  conversion_rate_delta  numeric,
  active_alerts          bigint,
  data_sources           bigint
)
language plpgsql
stable
security invoker
set search_path = ''
as $$
declare
  period_start timestamptz := date_trunc('day', now()) - make_interval(days => window_days);
  prior_start  timestamptz := date_trunc('day', now()) - make_interval(days => window_days * 2);
begin
  if not public.is_workspace_member(target_workspace) then
    raise exception 'Not a member of that workspace';
  end if;

  return query
  with
  -- Current and prior window totals for each daily metric, in one pass.
  windows as (
    select
      p.metric_key,
      sum(p.value) filter (where p.bucket >= period_start)                             as current_total,
      sum(p.value) filter (where p.bucket >= prior_start and p.bucket < period_start)  as prior_total
    from public.metric_points p
    where p.workspace_id = target_workspace
      and p.grain = 'day'
      and p.bucket >= prior_start
      and p.metric_key in ('revenue', 'active_users', 'events', 'signups', 'visitors')
    group by p.metric_key
  ),
  metric as (
    select
      coalesce(max(current_total) filter (where metric_key = 'revenue'), 0)      as revenue_now,
      coalesce(max(prior_total)   filter (where metric_key = 'revenue'), 0)      as revenue_prior,
      coalesce(max(current_total) filter (where metric_key = 'active_users'), 0) as users_now,
      coalesce(max(prior_total)   filter (where metric_key = 'active_users'), 0) as users_prior,
      coalesce(max(current_total) filter (where metric_key = 'events'), 0)       as events_now,
      coalesce(max(prior_total)   filter (where metric_key = 'events'), 0)       as events_prior,
      coalesce(max(current_total) filter (where metric_key = 'signups'), 0)      as signups_now,
      coalesce(max(prior_total)   filter (where metric_key = 'signups'), 0)      as signups_prior,
      coalesce(max(current_total) filter (where metric_key = 'visitors'), 0)     as visitors_now,
      coalesce(max(prior_total)   filter (where metric_key = 'visitors'), 0)     as visitors_prior
    from windows
  ),
  counts as (
    select
      (select count(*) from public.alerts a
        where a.workspace_id = target_workspace and a.is_active)        as alert_count,
      (select count(*) from public.data_sources d
        where d.workspace_id = target_workspace
          and d.status <> 'error')                                      as source_count
  )
  select
    m.revenue_now,
    public.pct_change(m.revenue_now, m.revenue_prior),
    -- active_users is stored per day; the window figure is the daily average
    -- rather than a sum, since summing would double-count returning users.
    round(m.users_now / greatest(window_days, 1)::numeric, 0),
    public.pct_change(m.users_now, m.users_prior),
    m.events_now,
    public.pct_change(m.events_now, m.events_prior),
    case when m.visitors_now = 0 then 0
         else round((m.signups_now / m.visitors_now) * 100, 2) end,
    public.pct_change(
      case when m.visitors_now   = 0 then 0 else m.signups_now   / m.visitors_now   end,
      case when m.visitors_prior = 0 then 0 else m.signups_prior / m.visitors_prior end
    ),
    c.alert_count,
    c.source_count
  from metric m cross join counts c;
end;
$$;

-- Percentage change with the usual divide-by-zero and "grew from nothing"
-- cases handled once, rather than at four call sites.
create or replace function public.pct_change(current_value numeric, prior_value numeric)
returns numeric
language sql
immutable
set search_path = ''
as $$
  select case
    when prior_value is null or prior_value = 0 then
      case when coalesce(current_value, 0) = 0 then 0 else 100 end
    else round(((coalesce(current_value, 0) - prior_value) / abs(prior_value)) * 100, 2)
  end;
$$;

grant execute on function public.get_dashboard_kpis(uuid, integer) to authenticated;

-- Nova Analytics — 0006_seed
--
-- Populates a workspace with demo content so the dashboard has something to
-- render before real ingestion exists (phase 5).
--
-- Exposed as a function rather than a bare INSERT script so it can be:
--   * called for any workspace, not just whichever one existed at migration
--     time,
--   * re-run safely (every write is an upsert or guarded by NOT EXISTS),
--   * called from the app when a brand-new workspace would otherwise show an
--     empty dashboard.
--
-- Running this file seeds every existing workspace once, at the bottom.

create or replace function public.seed_workspace_demo_data(target_workspace uuid)
returns void
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
declare
  day_offset  integer;
  hour_offset integer;
  bucket_day  timestamptz;
  -- Deterministic per-workspace jitter so two workspaces don't look identical
  -- but a given workspace is stable across re-runs.
  seed_base   numeric := (('x' || substr(md5(target_workspace::text), 1, 8))::bit(32)::bigint % 1000) / 1000.0;
  weekday     integer;
  seasonal    numeric;
  trend       numeric;
  visitors    numeric;
  signups     numeric;
begin
  if target_workspace is null then
    return;
  end if;

  -- --- data sources --------------------------------------------------------
  insert into public.data_sources
    (workspace_id, name, kind, status, platforms, events_30d, health_pct, last_sync_at)
  select target_workspace, v.name, v.kind, v.status, v.platforms, v.events_30d, v.health, now() - v.sync_ago
  from (values
    ('Web Analytics',   'web',       'active', array['apple','android','windows'], 2458000, 99.2, interval '4 minutes'),
    ('Mobile SDK',      'mobile',    'active', array['apple','android'],           1485000, 97.4, interval '11 minutes'),
    ('Billing Events',  'billing',   'active', array['windows'],                   1024000, 99.9, interval '2 minutes'),
    ('Checkout Funnel', 'web',       'active', array['apple','android','windows'],  858000, 95.0, interval '7 minutes'),
    ('Product API',     'api',       'active', array['apple','android','windows'], 3170000, 98.1, interval '1 minute'),
    ('Warehouse Sync',  'warehouse', 'error',  array['apple'],                       91200, 12.0, interval '3 days')
  ) as v(name, kind, status, platforms, events_30d, health, sync_ago)
  where not exists (
    select 1 from public.data_sources d
    where d.workspace_id = target_workspace and d.name = v.name
  );

  -- --- reports -------------------------------------------------------------
  insert into public.reports (workspace_id, name, status, schedule, completion, last_run_at)
  select target_workspace, v.name, v.status, v.schedule, v.completion, now() - v.ran_ago
  from (values
    ('Weekly Revenue Report', 'approved', '0 8 * * 1',  92.0, interval '2 days'),
    ('Churn Cohort Analysis', 'disabled', null,         41.0, interval '30 days'),
    ('Warehouse Sync',        'error',    '0 * * * *',  18.0, interval '3 days'),

-- Nova Analytics — 0005_rpc
--
-- get_dashboard_kpis: the six-tile row at the top of the dashboard, plus
-- period-over-period deltas, in one round trip.
--
-- Six separate queries for one card row is the obvious thing to get wrong —
-- it is also six chances for the tiles to disagree with each other if data
-- shifts mid-render. One call, one snapshot.

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Percentage change, with the divide-by-zero and "grew from nothing" cases
-- handled once rather than at four call sites.
--
-- Defined before get_dashboard_kpis because it is called from that body.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create or replace function public.pct_change(current_value numeric, prior_value numeric)
returns numeric
language sql
immutable
set search_path = ''
as $$
  select case
    when prior_value is null or prior_value = 0 then
      case when coalesce(current_value, 0) = 0 then 0 else 100 end
    else round(((coalesce(current_value, 0) - prior_value) / abs(prior_value)) * 100, 2)
  end;
$$;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The KPI row
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create or replace function public.get_dashboard_kpis(
  target_workspace uuid,
  window_days      integer default 30
)
returns table (
  monthly_revenue        numeric,
  monthly_revenue_delta  numeric,
  active_users           numeric,
  active_users_delta     numeric,
  events_tracked         numeric,
  events_tracked_delta   numeric,
  conversion_rate        numeric,
  conversion_rate_delta  numeric,
  active_alerts          bigint,
  data_sources           bigint
)
language plpgsql
stable
security invoker
set search_path = ''
as $$
declare
  period_start timestamptz := date_trunc('day', now()) - make_interval(days => window_days);
  prior_start  timestamptz := date_trunc('day', now()) - make_interval(days => window_days * 2);
begin
  -- Belt and braces: metric_points RLS already scopes reads to the caller's
  -- workspaces, but failing loudly beats silently returning zeros for a
  -- workspace the caller cannot see.
  if not public.is_workspace_member(target_workspace) then
    raise exception 'Not a member of that workspace';
  end if;

  return query
  with
  -- Current and prior window totals for every daily metric, in one pass.
  metric_windows as (
    select
      p.metric_key,
      sum(p.value) filter (where p.bucket >= period_start)                            as current_total,
      sum(p.value) filter (where p.bucket >= prior_start and p.bucket < period_start) as prior_total
    from public.metric_points p
    where p.workspace_id = target_workspace
      and p.grain = 'day'
      and p.bucket >= prior_start
      and p.metric_key in ('revenue', 'active_users', 'events', 'signups', 'visitors')
    group by p.metric_key
  ),
  metric as (
    select
      coalesce(max(current_total) filter (where metric_key = 'revenue'), 0)      as revenue_now,
      coalesce(max(prior_total)   filter (where metric_key = 'revenue'), 0)      as revenue_prior,
      coalesce(max(current_total) filter (where metric_key = 'active_users'), 0) as users_now,
      coalesce(max(prior_total)   filter (where metric_key = 'active_users'), 0) as users_prior,
      coalesce(max(current_total) filter (where metric_key = 'events'), 0)       as events_now,
      coalesce(max(prior_total)   filter (where metric_key = 'events'), 0)       as events_prior,
      coalesce(max(current_total) filter (where metric_key = 'signups'), 0)      as signups_now,
      coalesce(max(prior_total)   filter (where metric_key = 'signups'), 0)      as signups_prior,
      coalesce(max(current_total) filter (where metric_key = 'visitors'), 0)     as visitors_now,
      coalesce(max(prior_total)   filter (where metric_key = 'visitors'), 0)     as visitors_prior
    from metric_windows
  ),
  counts as (
    select
      (select count(*) from public.alerts a
        where a.workspace_id = target_workspace and a.is_active)   as alert_count,
      (select count(*) from public.data_sources d
        where d.workspace_id = target_workspace
          and d.status <> 'error')                                 as source_count
  )
  select
    m.revenue_now,
    public.pct_change(m.revenue_now, m.revenue_prior),
    -- active_users is a daily figure, so the headline is the daily average
    -- over the window. Summing would count a returning user once per day.
    round(m.users_now / greatest(window_days, 1)::numeric, 0),
    public.pct_change(m.users_now, m.users_prior),
    m.events_now,
    public.pct_change(m.events_now, m.events_prior),
    case when m.visitors_now = 0 then 0
         else round((m.signups_now / m.visitors_now) * 100, 2) end,
    public.pct_change(
      case when m.visitors_now   = 0 then 0 else m.signups_now   / m.visitors_now   end,
      case when m.visitors_prior = 0 then 0 else m.signups_prior / m.visitors_prior end
    ),
    c.alert_count,
    c.source_count
  from metric m cross join counts c;
end;
$$;

revoke execute on function public.pct_change(numeric, numeric) from public;
revoke execute on function public.get_dashboard_kpis(uuid, integer) from public;
grant execute on function public.pct_change(numeric, numeric) to authenticated;
grant execute on function public.get_dashboard_kpis(uuid, integer) to authenticated;

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Apply every migration to a throwaway Postgres and assert the behaviour that
# matters — the signup trigger, seed idempotency, and RLS tenant isolation.
#
# Run this before pasting migrations into a Supabase project. Postgres will
# happily accept a policy that leaks data across tenants; syntax being valid
# proves nothing.
#
#   ./supabase/tests/run-migration-tests.sh
#
# Requires Docker. Nothing touches your Supabase project.

set -euo pipefail

CONTAINER="nova-pg-test-$$"
IMAGE="postgres:16-alpine"
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"

cleanup() { docker rm -f "$CONTAINER" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; }
trap cleanup EXIT

echo "==> starting throwaway postgres"
docker run -d --name "$CONTAINER" -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=test "$IMAGE" >/dev/null

for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
  docker exec "$CONTAINER" pg_isready -U postgres >/dev/null 2>&1 && break
  sleep 1
done

run_sql() {
  docker cp "$1" "$CONTAINER:/tmp/current.sql" >/dev/null
  docker exec -i "$CONTAINER" psql -U postgres -d postgres \
    -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 --quiet -f /tmp/current.sql
}

echo "==> installing Supabase shim (auth schema, auth.uid, roles)"
run_sql "$ROOT/supabase/tests/shim.sql" >/dev/null

echo "==> applying migrations"
for migration in "$ROOT"/supabase/migrations/*.sql; do
  printf '    %-24s' "$(basename "$migration")"
  run_sql "$migration" >/dev/null
  echo "ok"
done

echo "==> re-applying migrations (must be idempotent)"
for migration in "$ROOT"/supabase/migrations/*.sql; do
  printf '    %-24s' "$(basename "$migration")"
  run_sql "$migration" >/dev/null
  echo "ok"
done

echo "==> assertions"
run_sql "$ROOT/supabase/tests/assertions.sql"

echo
echo "All migration tests passed."

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Apply every migration to a throwaway Postgres and assert the behaviour that
# matters — the signup trigger, seed idempotency, and RLS tenant isolation.
#
# Run this before pasting migrations into a Supabase project. Postgres will
# happily accept a policy that leaks data across tenants; syntax being valid
# proves nothing.
#
#   ./supabase/tests/run-migration-tests.sh
#
# Requires Docker. Nothing touches your Supabase project.

set -euo pipefail

CONTAINER="nova-pg-test-$$"
IMAGE="postgres:16-alpine"
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"

cleanup() { docker rm -f "$CONTAINER" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; }
trap cleanup EXIT

echo "==> starting throwaway postgres"
docker run -d --name "$CONTAINER" -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=test "$IMAGE" >/dev/null

for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
  docker exec "$CONTAINER" pg_isready -U postgres >/dev/null 2>&1 && break
  sleep 1
done

run_sql() {
  docker cp "$1" "$CONTAINER:/tmp/current.sql" >/dev/null
  docker exec -i "$CONTAINER" psql -U postgres -d postgres \
    -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 --quiet -f /tmp/current.sql
}

echo "==> installing Supabase shim (auth schema, auth.uid, roles)"
run_sql "$ROOT/supabase/tests/shim.sql" >/dev/null

echo "==> applying migrations"
for migration in "$ROOT"/supabase/migrations/*.sql; do
  printf '    %-24s' "$(basename "$migration")"
  run_sql "$migration" >/dev/null
  echo "ok"
done

echo "==> re-applying migrations (must be idempotent)"
for migration in "$ROOT"/supabase/migrations/*.sql; do
  printf '    %-24s' "$(basename "$migration")"
  run_sql "$migration" >/dev/null
  echo "ok"
done

echo "==> assertions"
run_sql "$ROOT/supabase/tests/assertions.sql"

echo
echo "All migration tests passed."

1	# Nova Analytics
2	
3	The Nova Analytics web app: a marketing landing page, email/password
4	authentication, and a whitelabeled analytics dashboard.
5	
6	```
7	/                    Landing page (public)
8	/auth/sign-in        Sign in
9	/auth/sign-up        Create account
10	/admin/*             Dashboard — requires an authenticated session
11	```
12	
13	---
14	
15	## Setup
16	
17	Requires **Node.js 18+** (LTS recommended) and npm.
18	
19	```bash
20	git clone <this-repo>
21	cd nova-analytics-dashboard
22	npm install
23	cp .env.example .env.local     # then fill in the values — see below
24	npm start                      # http://localhost:3000
25	```
26	
27	Other scripts:
28	
29	| Command | What it does |
30	| --- | --- |
31	| `npm run dev` (or `npm start`) | Vite dev server on port 3000 |
32	| `npm run build` | Production bundle into `dist/` |
33	| `npm run preview` | Serve the production build locally on port 3000 |
34	| `npm run pretty` | Prettier over `src/**/*.{js,jsx,json}` |
35	
36	There is no test script — no test runner is configured yet. See Limitations.
37	
38	### Environment variables
39	
40	**You need to supply these — they are not in the repo and nothing is
41	hardcoded.** Copy `.env.example` to `.env.local` and fill in:
42	
43	| Variable | Where to get it | Required |
44	| --- | --- | --- |
45	| `VITE_SUPABASE_URL` | Supabase dashboard → Project Settings → Data API → Project URL | Yes, for auth |
46	| `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` | Same page → Project API keys → `anon` `public` | Yes, for auth |
47	
48	Notes:
49	
50	- Vite only exposes variables prefixed with `VITE_`, and it **inlines them at
51	  build time**. Restart the dev server after editing
52	  `.env.local`; changing them requires a rebuild, not just a redeploy.
53	- The anon key is designed to be public and shipped in a browser bundle. It
54	  is not a secret. What actually protects your data is **Row Level Security**
55	  on every table — enable it before storing anything real.
56	- Never put the `service_role` key in this file or anywhere in the frontend.
57	- `.env.local` is gitignored. `.env.example` is committed and contains
58	  placeholders only.
59	
60	### Supabase project setup
61	
62	1. Create a project at [supabase.com](https://supabase.com).
63	2. **Authentication → Providers → Email**: enable it. Email/password is all
64	   this app uses; no OAuth provider is wired up.
65	3. **Authentication → URL Configuration → Site URL**: `http://localhost:3000`
66	   for local development; your real origin before deploying.
67	4. **Authentication → URL Configuration → Redirect URLs**: add
68	   `http://localhost:3000/**` (and `https://your-domain/**` for production).
69	   **This is required.** Every emailed link redirects to `/auth/callback`, and
70	   Supabase silently falls back to the Site URL if that path is not
71	   allow-listed — the link then appears to do nothing.
72	5. **Authentication → Email → Confirm email**: your call. Both are handled.
73	   - **On** (Supabase default): sign-up shows a "check your inbox" message
74	     with a resend option; the emailed link lands on `/auth/callback`, which
75	     establishes the session and forwards into the dashboard.
76	   - **Off**: sign-up returns a session immediately and goes straight to the
77	     dashboard.
78	6. **Run the database migrations**: paste each file in
79	   `supabase/migrations/` into the SQL Editor **in numeric order** and run it.
80	   They are idempotent, so re-running is safe.
81	
82	   | Migration | What it adds |
83	   | --- | --- |
84	   | `0001_profiles` | `profiles`, RLS, profile-on-signup trigger |
85	   | `0002_workspaces` | `workspaces`, `workspace_members`, `workspace_invites`, membership helpers, workspace-on-signup |
86	   | `0003_domain` | `data_sources`, `reports`, `alerts`, `tasks`, `notifications` |
87	   | `0004_metrics` | `events` (phase 5) and `metric_points` + `get_metric_series` |
88	   | `0005_rpc` | `get_dashboard_kpis` |
89	   | `0006_seed` | `seed_workspace_demo_data`, then seeds existing workspaces |
90	
91	   Verify them locally first with `./supabase/tests/run-migration-tests.sh`
92	   (see Testing below).
93	7. Supabase's built-in SMTP is heavily rate-limited (a few messages per hour)
94	   and intended only for testing. Configure your own SMTP before any real
95	   signup volume.
96	
97	If the two env vars are missing the app still builds and runs — the landing
98	page works, and the auth screens render with an explanatory banner and
99	disabled submit buttons rather than crashing.
100	
101	---
102	
103	## Tech stack
104	
105	| Layer | Choice | Why |
106	| --- | --- | --- |
107	| UI | React 19 | Already the base of the template this product is derived from; no reason to churn it. |
108	| Build | Vite 8 | Migrated off the inherited Create React App, which is deprecated and carried transitive CVEs. Build went from ~40s to ~0.6s, and route-level code splitting became straightforward. |
109	| Routing | React Router 6 | Inherited; `ProtectedRoute` composes cleanly with its element API. |
110	| Styling | Tailwind CSS 3 | Inherited, and the brand kit maps onto a token-based utility system almost directly. |
111	| Charts | ApexCharts via `react-apexcharts` | Inherited. Colors now come from the brand kit's `dataviz-categorical` palette. |
112	| Auth | Supabase Auth (`@supabase/supabase-js` v2) | Requested. Hosted email/password with session persistence and refresh handled for us — no backend to run. |
113	| Icons | `react-icons` | Inherited. |
114	
115	### Where things live
116	
117	```
118	nova_analytics_id/        Brand kit — logos, color/type tokens, guidelines
119	src/
120	  assets/img/layout/nova/ Nova logo SVGs + favicon source
121	  components/
122	    auth/ProtectedRoute   Session gate for /admin/*
123	    brand/NovaLogo        Inline-SVG logo (mark | horizontal | stacked)
124	  contexts/AuthContext    Session + profile state, all auth actions
125	  lib/supabase.js         Supabase client, reads env vars
126	  views/
127	    landing/              Marketing page and its sections
128	    auth/                 SignIn, SignUp, AuthCallback, ResetPassword
129	    admin/                Dashboard, data tables, profile
130	  routes.js               Sidebar + router route table
131	supabase/migrations/      SQL to run in the Supabase SQL Editor
132	tailwind.config.js        Nova design tokens
133	```
134	
135	### Design tokens
136	
137	`tailwind.config.js` is the single source of truth for color. It reads from
138	the brand kit anchors and exposes:
139	
140	- `primary-*` (indigo, `500` = `#4F46E5`), also aliased as `brand-*`
141	- `accent-*` (spark cyan, `500` = `#22D3EE`)
142	- `neutral-*` (Nova gray ramp), also aliased as `gray-*`
143	- `amber-*` (secondary accent), `success` / `warning` / `danger` / `info`
144	- `navy-*` — the dark-mode surface ramp, running ink → indigo-darker
145	
146	Fonts: `font-display` (Space Grotesk), `font-sans` (Inter, the default), and
147	`font-mono` (JetBrains Mono, used for metrics, tables and code). Loaded from
148	Google Fonts in `src/index.css`, which also re-exports every token as a CSS
149	custom property (`--nova-indigo`, `--nova-font-body`, …).
150	
151	The brand kit specifies anchor values, not full ramps. Intermediate steps
152	(`primary` 50–400, `neutral` 200/400/600/800, `accent` 600–900) are
153	interpolated in `tailwind.config.js` and marked as such in comments.
154

156	
157	## Known limitations and shortcuts

content.text:
Phases 0–2 are done and committed. Stopping here to hand back before the frontend work, since there's a decision you need to make.

## Done

**Phase 0 — Vite migration.** `react-scripts` out (1158 packages), Vite 8 in. Build went 40s → 0.6s. The gotchas the plan flagged were real: `routes.js` and `index.js` needed `.jsx` extensions, and three imports referenced `routes.js` by filename.

I also split the route table into `adminRoutes`/`authRoutes`. Both layouts shared one table, so the **sign-in page was loading ApexCharts and every dashboard component**. Bundle now:

| Route | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Landing | 300 kB | 129 kB |
| Sign-in | +169 kB | **+5 kB** |
| Dashboard | — | 169 kB, only when reached |

**Phase 1 — Vercel.** `vercel.json` with SPA rewrite, immutable asset caching, security headers. Verified deep links against a real preview build. Note: I left `comment` keys out — Vercel validates strictly and an unknown key fails the build rather than being ignored.

**Phase 2 — Schema.** Five migrations: workspaces/members/invites, the five domain tables, `metric_points` + `events`, `get_dashboard_kpis`, and a re-runnable seed.

## The part I want to flag

I didn't hand you five files of unvalidated SQL. Docker was available, so I built a harness (`supabase/tests/`) that spins up real Postgres with a Supabase shim, applies every migration twice, and asserts behaviour. It caught two things I'd otherwise have shipped:

- **`SET LOCAL` outside a transaction is silently a no-op** — my isolation checks were running as superuser and passing for the wrong reason. Genuinely dangerous: the tests were green while proving nothing.
- The `data_sources` KPI excluded errored sources, so the tile said 5 while the table below it showed 6.

I then deliberately broke a policy to `using (true)` and confirmed the suite fails — a green isolation test that can't detect a leak is worse than no test.

```
./supabase/tests/run-migration-tests.sh   # requires Docker, touches nothing remote
```

## Your call before I continue

Phase 3–4 wire the frontend to this schema. But **you have to run the migrations in the Supabase SQL editor first** — I can't run DDL with a publishable key, and I'm not going to ask for your `service_role` key.

Two things worth deciding:

1. **The seed writes demo data into your real project.** `0006_seed.sql` seeds every existing workspace with 6 sources, 4 reports, 90 days of metrics. That's what makes the dashboard look alive — but it's fake data in a production project. If you'd rather keep it clean, skip `0006` and I'll wire the empty states instead (they're already verified to return zeros cleanly).

2. **Landing page still claims "SOC 2 Type II" and 99.98% uptime.** Now that `workspaces.plan` exists, the pricing tiers could become real. The compliance claim should come off before this is public regardless.

I can start Phase 3 immediately — the query layer and `WorkspaceContext` don't need the migrations applied to be written, only to be tested.

content.text:
I wrote all of this copy as placeholder, and the SOC 2 line isn't the only one — there are ~15 claims in the same category. Full inventory:

**Specific verifiable falsehoods** (highest risk)
| Claim | Where | Reality |
|---|---|---|
| "SOC 2 Type II" | Hero | A named third-party audit certification |
| "99.98% platform uptime" | Stats band | Implies an SLA; nothing is measured |
| "<400ms median query time" | Stats band | Never benchmarked |
| "5.7M events ingested daily" | Stats band | Zero events ingested |
| "24 native integrations" | Stats band | Zero |

**Capabilities that don't exist**
- "Real-time pipelines now in beta" — no pipeline at all
- "columnar store tuned for event data" — it's plain Postgres
- "cohorts and funnels over hundreds of millions of rows"
- "Anomalies find you" — also inside the app, on the sidebar card
- "Funnels and retention built in", "attribution"
- "SSO, audit logs, EU or US data residency" — none implemented (`data_residency` is a column that does nothing)
- "Connect Postgres, Stripe, your product SDK and ad platforms"

**Actually true today:** row-level permissions (RLS, workspace-scoped, tested), "no credit card required", and "14-day trial" is backed by a real `trial_ends_at` default.

SOC 2 is the one with teeth — it's a specific audited certification, and enterprise buyers make purchasing decisions on it. But shipping a page that fixes only that line while still claiming 99.98% uptime and 24 integrations doesn't really solve the problem.

content.text:
Done. The claim is gone, along with the fourteen others in the same category.

## What changed

**Removed as present-tense claims:** SOC 2 Type II, 99.98% uptime, <400ms query time, 5.7M events/day, 24 integrations, columnar store, anomaly detection, SSO, audit logs, data residency, Slack routing, "hundreds of millions of rows".

**Kept, as a labelled roadmap band** where the fake stats used to be — SOC 2, SSO/audit logs, EU/US residency, and event ingestion, each with a `PLANNED` chip. The SOC 2 entry reads *"Not yet certified. On the path, not a claim we make today."*

**Pricing** features became objects with a `planned` flag, so SSO and residency render a chip instead of sitting silently among shipped features.

**Feature cards** now describe things that actually exist — shared metric definitions, RLS workspace isolation (genuinely the strongest thing here, and it's tested), the pre-wired dashboard, the source register.

Two things worth calling out:

**The same claim was inside the app.** The sidebar card promised "automatic anomaly detection across every metric you track" to people who'd already signed up. That's arguably worse than the marketing page — it's shown to paying users. Now points at the data source register.

**Claims that survived because they're true:** no credit card required, the 14-day trial (backed by a real `trial_ends_at` default), isolated workspace per team, never charged per viewer.

## The part that needs your judgement

I documented the Features/roadmap boundary in the README so it doesn't quietly erode — moving an item into Features or dropping its chip is a factual assertion, not a copy tweak.

Two things I left alone that are still yours to decide:

- **Pricing figures** ($0 / $390 / Custom) are intended pricing with no billing integration and no metering behind the event quotas. That's normal for pre-launch, but the Starter tier's "up to 3 data sources" isn't enforced anywhere.
- **"Dedicated success manager" and "Priority support"** are operational commitments — only you know if Nova can honour them.

The hero's preview card still shows `$340,512` and `24 Sources`, but that's illustrative product UI matching your seeded demo data, not a claim about the company — I'd leave it.

Phases 0–2 remain done. Ready to pick up Phase 3 (the query layer and `WorkspaceContext`) whenever — and since you've run `0006`, I can now verify against your real seeded data rather than a fake session.
